h1: Cylinder sizing, recovery and incoming water flow
title: Cylinder Sizing, Recovery & Water Flow | G3 Guide
description: Understand cylinder sizing, recovery and incoming water flow with clear model-aware information and practical questions for your cylinder engineer.
answer: Choose capacity and recovery around actual demand and the heat source, while measuring usable supply rather than relying on standing pressure alone.

sections.heading: The key distinction
paragraphs: The number of bathrooms is only one part of the assessment. Simultaneous use, shower flow, bath size, available reheating and normal schedules affect the volume of usable hot water. An oversized cylinder does not cure an inlet restriction or an inadequate supply.

sections.heading: Apply the information to the installed system
paragraphs: Replacement surveys also need space, full weight, access and a compliant discharge route. A universal litres-per-person table or a promised powerful shower cannot replace measured conditions and the selected model specification.

sections.heading: A practical next question
paragraphs: Gather the full model, heating method, recent symptoms and available paperwork. Discuss the scope with a person competent for the actual work. Technical information here supports that conversation and is not a substitute for manufacturer instructions or individual system assessment.

faqs.question: Will a larger cylinder always cure weak shower flow?
faqs.answer: No. Stored capacity and flow are different; the supply, restrictions and outlets must be assessed before a larger cylinder is proposed.
